# Meta Advertising Policies & Account Health (2025–2026)

Reviewed 2026-07-22 (lane caveats added 2026-09-29). Legitimate compliance only.

**Lane caveat (operator rule):** this file describes the clean-lane remedy (fix, appeal, request review, resubmit). On the operator's own BM, **on an ad disapproval do not edit or resubmit**: switch the ad off, leave it, report; account-level appeals are the operator's/TL's decision (`meta-grey-ops/23`, `05`).

Naming: policy book = **Meta Advertising Standards** (transparency.meta.com/policies/ad-standards/), not Business Help Center. **Account Quality** = **Business Support Home** (business.facebook.com/business-support-home); facebook.com/accountquality still resolves — same surface, old name in pre-2024 articles.

---

## 1. Structure of the Meta Advertising Standards

Top-level groups (Transparency Center, fetched 2026-07-22):

1. **Unacceptable content** (fully prohibited): CSEA/nudity, Coordinating Harm/Promoting Crime, Dangerous Orgs/Individuals, Discriminatory Practices, Hateful Conduct, Human Exploitation, Locally Illegal Content, Misinformation (fact-checker-debunked), Vaccine Discouragement.
2. **Fraud, Scams, Deceptive Practices**: incl. Unacceptable Business Practices. Meta may require **additional verification** for "potentially suspicious behavior" or categories likely scam targets.
3. **Restricted goods/services** (allowed with conditions/permission, §3): Alcohol, Commercial Exploitation of Crises, Dating, Hazardous Goods, Health and Wellness (weight loss/cosmetics/adult/reproductive), Historical Artifacts, Human Body Parts, Animals, Tobacco, Weapons/Ammunition/Explosives, Drugs and Pharmaceuticals, Drug & Alcohol Addiction Treatment, Financial/Insurance, Cryptocurrency, Online Gambling and Games.
4. **Objectionable content**: Adult Nudity/Sexual Activity/Exploitation/Solicitation, Bullying/Harassment, Profanity, Privacy Violations and **Personal Attributes**, Violent/Graphic Content, Suicide/Self-Injury/Eating Disorders.
5. **IP infringement**: third-party IP (incl. counterfeit), use of Meta IP/licenses.
6. **Social issue/electoral/political** (§4).
7. **Product/format-specific**: Video Ads (no flashing-screen tactics; entertainment trailers need written permission + 18+); **Lead Ads** (13 restricted question types, below); Targeting (no discriminatory/predatory use); Relevance (ad must match landing page); Branded Content (must tag partner).

Practitioner mapping: groups 1–2 + most of 4 = outright prohibition; group 3 = "restricted" — runs with conditions/age-gating/written permission.

Four stated principles: protect from unsafe/discriminatory practices; protect from fraud; promote positive UX (basis of negative-self-perception/sensational-content rules); promote transparency (Ad Library; political ads stored 7 years).

**Lead Ads restricted questions** (format-specific, often missed): without prior written permission, forms must not request account numbers, criminal history, financial info (bank/card, credit score, income, debt), government IDs (SSN, passport, license), health info, insurance info, **political affiliation (never allowed, no permission route)**, race/ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation, trade-union membership, usernames/passwords. Also banned: custom questions recreating what a Prefill Question already covers.

---

## 2. Personal Attributes, sensational content, "negative self-perception"

**Personal Attributes (official text):** ads must not assert/imply race, ethnicity, religion, beliefs, age, sexual orientation/practices, gender identity, disability, physical/mental health, vulnerable financial status, voting status, trade-union membership, criminal record, or name.

- Trigger: **"you" + sensitive attribute** — "Are you struggling with debt?", "Do you have diabetes?". "You" alone is fine; paired with a sensitive trait it isn't. [practitioner consensus, 2026-05]
- Fix: describe the **product**, not the person — "A care routine for thinning hair after 35" not "Are you 35 and balding?"
- Negative framing can imply a sensitive attribute; positive framing alone doesn't cure it.
- Distinguish from **Misleading/Unrealistic claims** (unverifiable outcome) and **Adult Content** (too much skin, even non-sexual) — one of the most confusing rejection reasons; Ads Manager label: "Personal Attributes."

**Negative self-perception (official, under Health and Wellness):** ads must not imply/generate negative self-perception or declare a "perfect body type" to sell diet/weight-loss/cosmetic/health products. Basis for before/after crackdown — imagery, copy, testimonials, or landing page can all violate it; moving the claim to a testimonial doesn't fix it. Remove problem-body emphasis, substantiate objective claims, review the full destination; appeal only after fixing the cited issue.

**Sensational/shocking content (official):** no "shocking, sensational or excessively violent content"; video ads must avoid disruptive tactics like flashing screens.

**Misleading/unrealistic claims:** guarantees, miracle claims, deceptive pricing, unsupported outcomes → rejection + enforcement risk. Qualified wording doesn't cure an otherwise misleading claim.

**20% text-on-image rule: retired.** Text density can still affect readability/performance but causes no automatic rejection/delivery penalty — pre-2024 posts citing a hard 20% limit are outdated.

---

## 3. Restricted verticals: rules and permission routes

**Alcohol** — local law/licenses/industry codes; age+country targeting per Meta/local law; **min 18+**; banned outright in some countries. No permission form, but no excessive-consumption depiction; video/entertainment restrictions apply.

**Online gambling and games** — official definition: "any product/service where anything of monetary value is included as part of a method of entry and prize" — sweeps in casinos, sportsbooks, poker, bingo, lotteries, **fantasy sports, sweepstakes casinos, skill-based/prize contests**. **Authorization required**, via **Authorizations and Verifications in Meta Business Suite**; approvals attach to **specific business portfolios/ad accounts**. Licence per targeted territory; declare intent for each new jurisdiction; 18+; strict geo-fencing. Affiliates/aggregators not exempt — a landing page referencing real-money play/bonuses/promo codes, or redirecting to an operator, counts as gambling. **19 unsupported markets for BOTH real-money and social casino**: Azerbaijan, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Egypt, Hong Kong, India, Indonesia, Korea, Kyrgyzstan, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar, Pakistan, Philippines, Saudi Arabia, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam. No US-state rule on Meta's page — state law governs. [official 2026-09-25, transparency.meta.com/policies/ad-standards/restricted-goods-services/gambling-games/] Context: Meta reports removing 159M+ scam ads in 2025, 92% pre-report.

**Dating** — "only allowed with prior written permission," apply via the form on the dating policy page; must follow dating targeting requirements/ad guidelines.

**Crypto/financial** — Crypto trading platforms/software enabling monetisation/reselling/swapping/staking require **prior written permission**; not every crypto ad needs it (educational content, hardware wallets, tax services exempt) [official, transparency.meta.com/policies/ad-standards/restricted-goods-services/cryptocurrency-products-and-services/, 2026-09-25]. Financial/insurance (credit cards, loans, insurance): **18+ min**, must not directly request PII/financial info in-ad; may require identity/regulator-authorization verification; statutory disclosures apply. **Drug & alcohol addiction treatment (US)**: requires **LegitScript certification** + Meta permission application.

**Supplements/health claims** — no ads for "illicit/recreational drugs or other unsafe substances/products/supplements as determined by Meta at its sole discretion"; prescription/OTC/cannabis-derived have category-specific rules. **Weight loss/dietary/health: 18+ mandatory. Cosmetic products/procedures/surgeries: 18+ mandatory.** No negative self-perception/before-after (§2); no unverifiable medical claims. Gotcha: a shared domain inherits risk — compliant cosmetics + non-compliant supplements on one domain can get the whole domain's ads rejected.

**Subscriptions** — no standalone category in current standards; auto-renew/free-trial offers policed under Unacceptable Business Practices / Fraud-Scams-Deceptive; recurring-charge terms must be disclosed, "free" claims hiding billing trigger rejection. FTC click-to-cancel rule (finalized Oct 2024) was vacated by the 8th Circuit 2025-07-08; exposure remains ROSCA / FTC Act §5 / state auto-renewal laws [legal, verify]. [uncertain — no dedicated Meta subscription policy found; treat FTC-style disclosure as the safe bar]

**Adult content** — no nudity/sexually suggestive positions/solicitation/explicit language. Adult products/reproductive health fall under Health and Wellness (18+, heavy creative constraints). Common false positive: innocent skin-showing visuals (swimwear, fitness) flagged as "Adult Content."

**Tobacco/weapons** — tobacco/nicotine/vape/paraphernalia prohibited (only WHO/FDA-approved cessation products allowed, local-law compliant). Weapons/ammunition/explosives/modification accessories prohibited.

## 4. Special Ad Categories

Four categories, **self-declared at campaign level** (dropdown, "Special Ad Category"): **Financial Products and Services** (renamed/broadened from "Credit" **Oct 2024** — now banking/insurance/loans/investments), **Employment**, **Housing**, **Social Issues, Elections, or Politics**.

- Required based on ad content + advertiser country + targeted countries — restriction matrix differs by jurisdiction.
- Targeting restrictions (Financial/Employment/Housing) can limit age, gender, postcode/radius, detailed targeting, lookalikes, saved audiences, custom-audience use, instant-form questions — varies by category/jurisdiction. **15-mile radius / no-ZIP** restriction is US anti-discrimination specific — don't apply worldwide. Special Ad Audiences discontinued.
- **Social Issues/Elections/Politics**: requires identity **authorization** (advertiser must reside in targeted country), **"Paid for by" disclaimer** linked to a Page, Ad Library storage **7 years**. Sweeps in non-political brands touching debated topics (healthcare, climate, immigration-adjacent messaging).
- **2025-01-13**: domains tied to special-ad-category-implying data (health, financial) saw **Pixel/CAPI data-sharing restrictions** — verify current state in Events Manager, rollout progressive.
- Failure to declare → rejection/enforcement risk. Don't declare reflexively or route around the requirement — compare offer against current official category definition.
- **EU/EEA DSA duties (ads transparency):** EU-targeted ads require declared
  `dsa_beneficiary` + `dsa_payor` at creation (API-enforced — spec rejected
  without them; `meta-grey-ops` launch defaults). Separately, EU social-issue /
  election / political ads are blocked since Oct 2025 (TTPA). Verify current
  Ads Manager fields live — DSA surface changes without API version bumps.

---

## 5. Ad review process

- Primarily automated, manual in some cases; starts before the ad runs, status "In review." **Typically <24h**, sometimes longer (practitioner: minutes–few hours common, manual/complex 24–48h+).
- Reviews ad components (image/video/text/**audio**), **targeting**, and **landing page/destination** incl. redirect paths.
- **Re-review at any time** — approved ads can be rejected later, even after going live; an edited ad is a **new ad**, re-reviewed.
- Meta also reviews **business assets** (portfolio, ad accounts, Pages, user accounts) and restricts at any level. A restricted *user* doesn't block other admins of the same account/business from advertising.

---

## 6. Recurring rejection causes

Vendor rejection/appeal rates aren't portable across markets/verticals/periods — diagnose from the exact policy code + affected destination.

Creative: before/after transformation imagery; zoomed "problem" body parts; text-heavy creative (20% rule retired — don't attribute rejection to text density without the displayed reason); translated/regional copy breaking compliance; negative emotional/personal-attribute framing; stacked currency symbols/excessive emoji ("low quality"); visuals resembling restricted categories (pharma crosses, bottle silhouettes, casino motifs).

Copy: "you" + sensitive attribute; guaranteed outcomes; unbacked medical claims ("cures", "doctor-approved"); financial guarantees ("guaranteed returns"); misleading discount math vs. landing page.

Targeting/account: Special Ad Category not declared; landing-page mismatch; domain sells restricted products elsewhere on the site; destination quality/redirect/broken pages/unverifiable offer; account history of repeated/severe violations (§7).

Rejection email is generic — real reason is in Ads Manager → hover "Not delivering" → "See details" for the policy code.

---

## 7. Why ad accounts get restricted or disabled

| Category | Triggers | First fix |
|---|---|---|
| Advertising Standards violation | Repeated/severe violations; restricted category run without permission; undeclared special ad category | Fix/remove offending ads, then appeal (operator lane: switch ads off, no edit or resubmit) |
| Business/payment verification | Required verification incomplete; billing can't be validated | Complete verification, resolve billing |
| Unusual/suspicious activity | Login anomalies, possible compromise, sudden behavior change | Secure account, confirm identity, 2FA |
| Circumventing systems | Evading review/prior enforcement — cloaking or replacement assets | Clean lane: stop workaround, preserve evidence, fix root issue, use supported review route. Grey execution → `meta-grey-ops` |
| Low ad-account quality | Accumulated disapprovals, high negative feedback | Reduce disapproval rate over time |

Payment-specific: repeated failed payments (expired/insufficient/decline) → automatic suspension; fast payment-method swapping looks suspicious. Some prepaid/virtual cards report more failures — no universal card-type ban published. Name mismatch (card vs account) is a trigger. Chargebacks can freeze billing/trigger review (investigate unauthorized charges first via Meta support; permanent ban possible but not documented as automatic). Meta may lower billing threshold/daily limit after declines. Failed transaction, payable balance, card verification/default status, payment-method eligibility, and account restriction are **independent facts** — `No payment due` does not erase a failed transaction or lift a restriction; never top up when nothing is owed.

Behavioral/structural: sudden spend/login change can coincide with risk review but **no official >20%/day threshold published**. Enforcement can propagate to connected people/accounts/Pages/portfolios depending on the violation — don't assume automatic "poisoning" without evidence from the specific restriction. Customer-feedback/commerce-quality signals can affect delivery/selling privileges — inspect live status, no universal fixed score threshold. Review eligibility/time limits depend on asset + reason — no universal reinstatement deadline.

**Circumventing Systems**: cloaking, obfuscated destinations, replacement assets to bypass a restriction — can trigger enforcement beyond the individual ad. Clean-lane remediation stays here; operational grey (filters, whites, replacement) → `meta-grey-ops`.

## 8. Appeals: Business Support Home flow

Path: Business Support Home → Account status overview → select restricted account/asset → reason → "What you can do." Also facebook.com/accountquality. Rejected ad: Ads Manager → rejected ad → request review, or same path via Business Support Home (clean lane only; operator lane: no ad-level review request, no edit, no resubmit).

Four remediation paths (by cause): (1) confirm identity (email/phone/ID/payment proof); (2) complete verification ("Start verification"); (3) enable 2FA ("Secure your account"); (4) request review (formal appeal).

- Official: account-restriction reviews typically **~48h**, can take longer — expectation, not SLA. Request limits/eligibility/deadlines depend on asset+reason — no universal 180-day cutoff.
- Fix the cited issue before appealing; preserve notification, policy code, asset ID, submission date.
- Effective appeal practice: fix root issue first; address the specific policy code, under ~200 words; reference exact ad language; attach landing-page URL + 1–2 line product description; don't resubmit the same flagged creative in parallel.
- If review button absent: document state, use only shown support routes — absence of a button doesn't itself prove a final decision.
- Billing appeals: provide ad-account ID, transaction/payment ID, current balance state, and **only last-4 digits** of old/replacement cards — never a token, app secret, full card number, CVV, or verification code.

---

## 9. Keeping an account healthy

- Complete business verification when required (Security Center/in-product prompt); match legal details to accepted documents; paths/eligible docs/attempt limits vary by account.
- Verify domains when a feature/policy flow requires it — not universal.
- 2FA for everyone with asset access (required portfolio-wide for some portfolios); least privilege, real named users, no shared logins.
- Stable authorized payment method, sufficient funds, consistent billing details; resolve disputes through Meta's process, don't treat disputes as an optimization tactic.
- Controlled launch: budgets the business can monitor, confirm billing/measurement, scale from observed economics — "warming" is not an official trust-building requirement.
- Asset due diligence before attaching an existing Page/data source/domain/account — don't assume every historical issue transfers.
- Pre-flight creatives/destinations; no universal strike-count threshold published.
- Watch feedback signals (ad hides/reports, post-purchase score); pause ads accumulating negative feedback.
- Submit concise evidence-backed appeals via the exposed path; avoid duplicate submissions. Replacement accounts to evade an active restriction compound enforcement risk.

---

## Gaps

- No dedicated Meta subscription/auto-renewal ad-disclosure policy found (covered indirectly under Unacceptable Business Practices).
- Date of the gambling-permission move to Business Suite (2025-07) — practitioner-sourced; the A&V route itself is official (2026-09-25).
- No universal numeric account-quality strike/appeal-success threshold published.
- "Account Quality" vs "Business Support Home" branding — full retirement vs. coexistence unconfirmed across locales.
- 2026-02-23 start date of the 19-market list — practitioner-sourced; the list itself is official (2026-09-25).
